takeaways: Amgen beat on both lines: $6.45 of adjusted EPS vs $5.76 expected, and $10.37 billion in revenue vs $10.06 billion (Investing.com). Product sales grew 8%, driven by volume, per the release.

The growers carried it: cholesterol drug Repatha rose 37% to $1.085 billion, bone drug Evenity rose 39% to $751 million, asthma drug Tezspire rose 43% to $538 million, lung-cancer drug Imdelltra rose 128% to $406 million and Uplizna rose 191% to $451 million.

The drag is cheap copycats: Prolia sales fell 45% to $632 million and Xgeva fell 47% to $288 million as biosimilars launched around the world, and that's what investors focused on after hours (Investing.com).

Full-year guidance is $38.9-39.7 billion in revenue and $22.90-23.70 in adjusted EPS; both midpoints sit a bit above analyst estimates (Investing.com). Free cash flow was $3.7 billion, down from $4.2 billion a year ago on working-capital timing.

The obesity shot MariTide is still in a stack of Phase 3 trials, with two more diabetes studies starting in Q4, per the release. No new data this quarter, so the big swing for the stock is still ahead.
verdict: Amgen beat by 69 cents and the stock still slipped after hours, which is biotech for 'nice, but what about Prolia?' The new drugs are growing fast enough to cover the biosimilar hole for now. The real plot twist is MariTide, and that episode hasn't aired yet.
